classification.difficultyReason: Students must translate practical descriptions into triangles, justify corresponding angles and choose corresponding heights, shadows or road distances. The hut requires relating perpendicular heights to base widths. Similarity is explicitly supplied as the method; the label amendment adds no demand.

content.prompt: In each part, you will need to draw a diagram and prove that two triangles are similar.

children.label: a
children.prompt: A stick 1.5 metres long leans against a wall and reaches 1 metre up the wall. How far up the wall will a ladder 10 metres long reach if it is parallel to the stick?

answer.worked:
Let the ladder reach $h$ metres up the wall. In the diagram, $AB$ is the stick and $CD$ is the ladder.

$\angle AOB=\angle COD=90^\circ$ (wall perpendicular to ground), and $\angle ABO=\angle CDO$ (corresponding angles, $AB\parallel CD$).

Therefore $\triangle AOB\sim\triangle COD$ (AAA).

Matching height and sloping length give
$$\begin{align*}\frac{OC}{OA}&=\frac{CD}{AB}\\\frac{h}{1}&=\frac{10}{1.5}\\h&=\frac{20}{3}=6\tfrac23.\end{align*}$$
The ladder reaches $6\tfrac23$ metres up the wall.

spec.description: Authored schematic of a vertical wall, horizontal ground and parallel stick and ladder.
spec.mathematics: OA=1 m, AB=1.5 m, CD=10 m, OC=h m; AB parallel CD.

children.label: b
children.prompt: A 3 metre high road-sign casts a shadow 1.4 metres long. How high is a telegraph pole that casts a shadow 3.5 metres long at the same time of day?

answer.worked:
Let $AB$ represent the road-sign and $DE$ the telegraph pole, with shadow ends $C$ and $F$. Let $DE=h$ metres.

$\angle ABC=\angle DEF=90^\circ$ (vertical objects on horizontal ground), and $\angle ACB=\angle DFE$ (the Sun has the same angle of elevation).

Therefore $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle DEF$ (AAA).

Matching height and shadow length give
$$\begin{align*}\frac{DE}{AB}&=\frac{EF}{BC}\\\frac{h}{3}&=\frac{3.5}{1.4}\\h&=3\times\frac{3.5}{1.4}\\h&=7.5.\end{align*}$$
The telegraph pole is $7.5$ metres high.

spec.description: Authored paired right triangles showing vertical objects and their horizontal shadows.
spec.mathematics: Sign height 3 m and shadow 1.4 m; pole height h m and shadow 3.5 m; equal solar elevation angles.

children.label: c
children.prompt: A steep road rises 1.2 metres for every 6 metres travelled along the road surface. How far will a car have to travel to rise 600 metres?

answer.worked:
Let $AC$ and $DF$ represent distances along the same straight road slope, and let $DF=d$ metres.

$\angle ABC=\angle DEF=90^\circ$ (vertical rise perpendicular to horizontal), and $\angle ACB=\angle DFE$ (the road has the same inclination).

Therefore $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle DEF$ (AAA).

Matching sloping distance and vertical rise give
$$\begin{align*}\frac{DF}{AC}&=\frac{DE}{AB}\\\frac{d}{6}&=\frac{600}{1.2}\\d&=6\times\frac{600}{1.2}\\d&=3000.\end{align*}$$
The car travels $3000$ metres along the road surface.

spec.description: Authored schematic paired slope triangles; road distances are labelled on the hypotenuses.
spec.mathematics: Vertical rises 1.2 m and 600 m correspond to road distances 6 m and d m.

children.label: d
children.prompt: The front of an A-frame hut is an isosceles triangle of height 5 metres and base 8 metres. How wide will a model of the hut be if its height is 0.8 metres?

answer.worked:
Let $ABC$ be the hut front and $DEF$ its scale model, with perpendicular heights $AG$ and $DH$. Let the model width be $w$ metres.

The model preserves the hut's angles. Thus $\angle ABC=\angle DEF$ and $\angle ACB=\angle DFE$, so $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle DEF$ (AAA).

The perpendicular heights also form matching right triangles: $\angle AGB=\angle DHE=90^\circ$ and $\angle ABG=\angle DEH$. Hence $\triangle AGB\sim\triangle DHE$ (AAA).

The height of each isosceles triangle bisects its base, so $BG=4$ and $EH=\frac{w}{2}$ metres. Matching sides give
$$\begin{align*}\frac{EH}{BG}&=\frac{DH}{AG}\\\frac{w/2}{4}&=\frac{0.8}{5}\\w&=8\times\frac{0.8}{5}\\w&=1.28.\end{align*}$$
The model is $1.28$ metres wide.

spec.description: Authored paired isosceles hut fronts with dashed perpendicular heights and labelled full widths.
spec.mathematics: Hut height 5 m, full base 8 m; similar model height 0.8 m, full base w m; heights bisect bases.
